title: Passenger Disgusted When Tesla Robotaxi Gets Stuck on "Fart Mode"
source_used: The San Francisco Standard (original report, 13 Oct 2026) and Futurism (relay, 16 Oct 2026)
key_facts: San Francisco Standard tech culture reporter Zara Stone rode a Tesla robotaxi in the Hayes Valley area of San Francisco on Monday night (12 Oct 2026) and it played fart sounds through its speakers.
The sounds come from Tesla's "emissions testing mode", a novelty feature added in a 2018 holiday software update.

The human safety driver said he did not know how long it would last, said he had been changing the settings when she summoned the car, and said he had lost control of the feature; even the volume did not control it.
The sounds had not stopped by the end of the ride, according to Stone.
Tesla's robotaxis are not yet licensed in California as fully autonomous vehicles like Waymo's, so a human driver must be at the wheel, though the cars mostly rely on Tesla's self-driving features.
Tesla did not respond to the Standard's request for comment.
Futurism relayed the story on 16 Oct 2026, mentioning an Instagram video of the ride.
quote_evidence: Not yet licensed in the state of California as fully autonomous vehicles like Waymo, the cars are required to have a human driver at the wheel, though they’re mostly relying on Tesla’s self-driving features.
They hadn’t stopped by the end of my ride, and I do not know if the next passenger was forced into flatulence or if the engineer managed to deactivate the feature in time.
Tesla did not respond to a request for comment.
why_it_matters_hint: A harmless but embarrassing software glitch in Tesla's still-supervised California robotaxi service, reported first-hand by one reporter.
notes: Original reporter is the San Francisco Standard; Futurism (the pool item) relays it. Both pages read in full. Ride date is before the 16 Oct 2026 window, so the entry is stale and the score is lowered. No safety problem is reported.
